wu: Warm-up: 'Tech Charades'—students draw tech-related words (e.g., 'smartphone', 'social media', 'download') from a hat and act them out while others guess. The actor says, 'I'm miming a tech word!' and the guessers respond, 'Is it a laptop?'
wuAlt: Alternative 1: 'Tech Word Association'—students shout out tech words starting with the last letter of the previous word (e.g., 'email → laptop → password').
Alternative 2: 'Quick Poll'—stand if you use social media daily, raise hands if you prefer online shopping, etc.
pres: Present verb patterns using a short story about 'Laila's tech habits': 'Laila stopped using TikTok to study.' 'She remembers to check her email.' 'She forgets to back up her files.' Model sentences on the board, then ask students to complete sentences like 'I remember to __' and 'I stopped __' to check understanding.
presAlt: Alternative 1: 'Realia Demo'—show a smartphone and say, 'I stopped using this app because it's distracting.' Then ask students to share their own examples.
Alternative 2: 'Picture Prompt'—show images of people using tech; elicit sentences like 'He remembers to charge his phone.'
prac: Guided practice: 'Verb Pattern Auction'—write sentences with errors (e.g., 'I stopped to play games') on slips. Teams bid to 'buy' correct sentences. The teacher says, 'The auction starts for this sentence!' and teams respond, 'We bid 2 dirhams for the correct one!'
pracAlt: Alternative 1: 'Sentence Race'—teams race to write correct sentences on the board using prompts like 'forget + to'.
Alternative 2: 'Matching Cards'—match verb phrases (e.g., 'stop scrolling') to the correct pattern (-ing or to + verb).
ls: Listening slot: Play a 2-minute clip of a debate about 'Are smartphones making us less social?' Students listen and circle all instances of 'stop/remember/forget + -ing/to'. Then they share one example with a partner, saying, 'I heard someone say, 'I stopped talking to people.''
re: Reactivation game: 'Tech Simon Says'—the teacher calls out commands like 'Simon says remember to charge your phone!' or 'Stop using your phones!' Students must obey only when 'Simon says' is included. Fast errors get a penalty (e.g., 10 jumping jacks).
prod: Production task: Split into 'For' and 'Against' panels to debate 'Should schools ban phones?' Each panel has 3 minutes to prepare arguments using verb patterns (e.g., 'We remember to use phones for research'). Then, each speaker presents their point for 1 minute, followed by a 2-minute Q&A where the audience asks, 'Do you agree that phones distract students?'
rw: Reading and writing slot: Read a short article about 'Digital Detox in Morocco' and underline all verb patterns. Then, write an 80-word paragraph for or against digital detoxes using at least 3 verb patterns. Example: 'I stopped scrolling social media to read more books. I remember to turn off my phone at 9 PM.'
st: Story + goodbye: Share a short story about 'Ali's weekend without Wi-Fi' highlighting verb patterns. End with the goodbye routine: 'Today we debated tech and practiced verb patterns—great work! Thank you, class.'
g: Teams bid on sentences with correct verb patterns (-ing or to)
Students act out tech words for others to guess
Obey commands only with 'Simon says' + verb patterns
Debate tech topics using target language
Teams race to write correct sentences on the board
diff: Fast finishers: Write a 100-word email to a friend explaining their tech habits using 5+ verb patterns.
Support: Use a sentence frame: 'I stopped ___. I remember to ___. I forget to ___.'
hw: Homework 1: Interview a family member about their tech habits and write 5 sentences using verb patterns.
Homework 2: Watch a 5-minute tech video and list 3 examples of 'stop/remember/forget + -ing/to'.
Homework 3: Write a 100-word paragraph: 'My relationship with technology' using at least 4 verb patterns.
tip: Tip: Encourage students to share Moroccan tech habits (e.g., using apps for haggling in souks) to make debates relatable and culturally relevant.
